references.text: Bethphage and Bethany are also mentioned in the parallel accounts of Jesus' entry into Jerusalem. See [ref:Matt 21:1|Matthew 21:1], where Jesus comes to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives and sends out two disciples.
Mark's parallel account of Jesus' arrival at Bethphage and Bethany on the Mount of Olives, where he sends two of his disciples ahead. See [ref:Mark 11:1|Mark 11:1].
Bethany is mentioned as a village near Jerusalem, confirming the geographical location in Luke's account. See [ref:Joh 11:18|John 11:18].
The Mount of Olives was a place where Jesus often stayed. Luke later notes that Jesus used to spend his nights on the Mount of Olives. See [ref:Luk 21:37|Luke 21:37].
The Mount of Olives is mentioned as the place where Jesus was taken up into heaven, just outside Jerusalem. See [ref:Apg 1:12|Acts 1:12].
A prophetic text stating that the Lord's feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem—the same mountain Jesus is now approaching. See [ref:Sak 14:4|Zechariah 14:4].
Here too, Jesus sends disciples out two by two ahead of him, a pattern repeated at the entry into Jerusalem. See [ref:Luk 10:1|Luke 10:1].
David went up to the Mount of Olives weeping as he fled from Absalom—a contrasting parallel to Jesus now coming to the Mount of Olives as king. See [ref:2 Sam 15:30|2 Samuel 15:30].
